1.1: And it comes to pass, after the death of Joshua, that the sons of Israel ask at Jehovah, saying, `Who does go up for us to the Canaanite, at the commencement, to fight against it?'
1.2: And Jehovah says, `Judah does go up; indeed, I have given the land into his hand.'
1.3: And Judah says to Simeon his brother, `Go up with me into my lot, and we fight against the Canaanite--and I have gone, even I, with you into your lot;' and Simeon goes with him.
1.4: And Judah goes up, and Jehovah gives the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hand, and they smite them in Bezek--ten thousand men;
1.5: and they find Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and fight against him, and smite the Canaanite and the Perizzite.
1.6: And Adoni-Bezek flees, and they pursue after him, and seize him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes,
1.7: and Adoni-Bezek says, `Seventy kings--their thumbs and their great toes cut off--have been gathering under my table; as I have done so has God repaid to me;' and they bring him in to Jerusalem, and he dies there.
1.8: And the sons of Judah fight against Jerusalem, and capture it, and smite it by the mouth of the sword, and the city they have sent into fire;
1.9: and afterwards have the sons of Judah gone down to fight against the Canaanite, inhabiting the hill-country, and the south, and the low country;
1.10: and Judah goes to the Canaanite who is dwelling in Hebron (and the name of Hebron formerly is Kirjath-Arba), and they smite Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.
1.11: And he goes from there to the inhabitants of Debir (and the name of Debir formerly is Kirjath-Sepher),
1.12: and Caleb says, `He who smites Kirjath-Sepher--and has captured it--then I have given to him Achsah my daughter for a wife.'
1.13: And Othniel son of Kenaz, younger brother of Caleb, does capture it, and he gives to him Achsah his daughter for a wife.
1.14: And it comes to pass in her coming in, that she persuades him to ask from her father the field, and she lights from off the ass, and Caleb says to her, `What--to you?'
1.15: And she says to him, `Give to me a blessing; when the south land you have given me--then you have given to me springs of water; and Caleb gives to her the upper springs and the lower springs.
1.16: And the sons of the Kenite, father-in-law of Moses, have gone up out of the city of palms with the sons of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad, and they go and dwell with the people.
1.17: And Judah goes with Simeon his brother, and they smite the Canaanite inhabiting Zephath, and devote it; and one calls the name of the city Hormah.
1.18: And Judah captures Gaza and its border, and Askelon and its border, and Ekron and its border;
1.19: and Jehovah is with Judah, and he occupies the hill-country, but not to dispossess the inhabitants of the valley, for they have chariots of iron.
1.20: And they give to Caleb Hebron, as Moses has spoken, and he dispossesses from there the three sons of Anak.
1.21: And the Jebusite, inhabiting Jerusalem, the sons of Benjamin have not dispossessed; and the Jebusite dwells with the sons of Benjamin, in Jerusalem, till this day.
1.22: And the house of Joseph go up--even they--to Beth-El, and Jehovah is with them;
1.23: and the house of Joseph cause men to spy about Beth-El (and the name of the city formerly is Luz),
1.24: and the watchers see a man coming out from the city, and say to him, `Show us, we pray you, the entrance of the city, and we have done with you kindness.'
1.25: And he shows them the entrance of the city, and they smite the city by the mouth of the sword, and the man and all his family they have sent away;
1.26: and the man goes to the land of the Hittites, and builds a city, and calls its name Luz--it is its name to this day.
1.27: And Manasseh has not occupied Beth-Shean and its towns, and Taanach and its towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Iblaim and its towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns, and the Canaanite is desirous to dwell in that land;
1.28: and it comes to pass, when Israel has been strong, that he sets the Canaanite to tribute, and has not utterly dispossessed it.
1.29: And Ephraim has not dispossessed the Canaanite who is dwelling in Gezer, and the Canaanite dwells in its midst, in Gezer.
1.30: Zebulun has not dispossessed the inhabitants of Kitron, and the inhabitants of Nahalol, and the Canaanite dwells in its midst, and they become tributary.
1.31: Asher has not dispossessed the inhabitants of Accho, and the inhabitants of Zidon, and Ahlab, and Achzib, and Helbah, and Aphik, and Rehob;
1.32: and the Asherite dwells in the midst of the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land, for it has not dispossessed them.
1.33: Naphtali has not dispossessed the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh, and the inhabitants of Beth-Anath, and he dwells in the midst of the Canaanite, the inhabitants of the land; and the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh and of Beth-Anath have become tributary to them.
1.34: And the Amorites press the sons of Dan to the mountain, for they have not suffered them to go down to the valley;
1.35: and the Amorite is desirous to dwell in mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim, and the hand of the house of Joseph is heavy, and they become tributary;
1.36: and the border of the Amorite is from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock and upward.

2.1: And a messenger of Jehovah goes up from Gilgal to Bochim,
2.2: and says, `I cause you to come up out of Egypt, and bring you in to the land which I have sworn to your fathers, and say, I do not break My covenant with you to the age; and you--you make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land--their altars you break down; and you have not hearkened to My voice--what is this you have done?
2.3: And I also have said, I do not cast them out from your presence, and they have been to you for adversaries, and their gods are to you for a snare.'
2.4: And it comes to pass, when the messenger of Jehovah speaks these words to all the sons of Israel, that the people lift up their voice and weep,
2.5: and they call the name of that place Bochim, and sacrifice there to Jehovah.
2.6: And Joshua sends the people away, and the sons of Israel go, each to his inheritance, to possess the land;
2.7: and the people serve Jehovah all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who prolonged days after Joshua, who saw all the great work of Jehovah which He did to Israel.
2.8: And Joshua son of Nun, servant of Jehovah, dies, a son of a hundred and ten years,
2.9: and they bury him in the border of his inheritance, in Timnath-Heres, in the hill-country of Ephraim, on the north of mount Gaash;
2.10: and also all that generation have been gathered to their fathers, and another generation rises after them who have not known Jehovah, and even the work which He has done to Israel.
2.11: And the sons of Israel do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and serve the Baalim,
2.12: and forsake Jehovah, God of their fathers, who brings them out from the land of Egypt, and go after other gods (of the gods of the peoples who are round about them), and bow themselves to them, and provoke Jehovah,
2.13: yes, they forsake Jehovah, and do service to Baal and to Ashtaroth.
2.14: And the anger of Jehovah burns against Israel, and He gives them into the hand of spoilers, and they spoil them, and He sells them into the hand of their enemies round about, and they have not been able any more to stand before their enemies;
2.15: in every place where they have gone out, the hand of Jehovah has been against them for evil, as Jehovah has spoken, and as Jehovah has sworn to them, and they are distressed--greatly.
2.16: And Jehovah raises up judges, and they save them from the hand of their spoilers;
2.17: and also to their judges they have not hearkened, but have gone a-whoring after other gods, and bow themselves to them; they have turned aside with haste out of the way in which their fathers walked to obey the commands of Jehovah--they have not done so.
2.18: And when Jehovah raised up to them judges--then was Jehovah with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for it repents Jehovah, because of their groaning from the presence of their oppressors, and of those thrusting them away.
2.19: And it has come to pass, at the death of the judge--they turn back and have done corruptly above their fathers, to go after other gods, to serve them, and to bow themselves to them; they have not fallen from their doings, and from their stiff way.
2.20: And the anger of Jehovah does burn against Israel, and He says, `Because that this nation have transgressed My covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened to My voice--
2.21: I also continue not to dispossess any from before them of the nations which Joshua has left when he dies,
2.22: in order to try Israel by them, whether they are keeping the way of Jehovah, to go in it, as their fathers kept it or not.'
2.23: And Jehovah leaves these nations, so as not to dispossess them hastily, and did not give them into the hand of Joshua.

3.1: And these are the nations which Jehovah left, to try Israel by them, all who have not known all the wars of Canaan;
3.2: (only for the sake of the generations of the sons of Israel's knowing, to teach them war, only those who formerly have not known them) --
3.3: five princes of the Philistines, and all the Canaanite, and the Zidonian, and the Hivite inhabiting mount Lebanon, from mount Baal-Hermon to the entering in of Hamath;
3.4: and they are to prove Israel by them, to know whether they obey the commands of Jehovah that He commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
3.5: And the sons of Israel have dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite, the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite,
3.6: and take their daughters to them for wives, and their daughters have given to their sons, and they serve their gods;
3.7: and the sons of Israel do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and forget Jehovah their God, and serve the Baalim and the shrines.
3.8: And the anger of Jehovah burns against Israel, and He sells them into the hand of Chushan-Rishathaim king of Aram-Naharaim, and the sons of Israel serve Chushan-Rishathaim eight years;
3.9: and the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah, and Jehovah raises a saviour to the sons of Israel, and he saves them--Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother;
3.10: and the Spirit of Jehovah is upon him, and he judges Israel, and goes out to battle, and Jehovah gives to his hand Chushan-Rishathaim king of Aram, and strong is his hand against Chushan-Rishathaim;
3.11: and the land rests forty years. And Othniel son of Kenaz dies,
3.12: and the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah; and Jehovah strengthens Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because that they have done the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah;
3.13: and he gathers to him the Bene-Ammon and Amalek, and goes and smites Israel, and they possess the city of palms;
3.14: and the sons of Israel serve Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
3.15: And the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah, and Jehovah raises to them a saviour, Ehud son of Gera, a Benjamite (a man--shut of his right hand), and the sons of Israel send by his hand a present to Eglon king of Moab;
3.16: and Ehud makes for himself a sword, and it has two mouths (a cubit is its length), and he girds it under his long robe on his right thigh;
3.17: and he brings near the present to Eglon king of Moab, and Eglon is a very fat man.
3.18: And it comes to pass, when he has finished to bring near the present, that he sends away the people bearing the present,
3.19: and he himself has turned back from the graven images which are at Gilgal, and says, `A secret word I have to you, O king;' and he says, `Hush!' and go out from him do all those standing by him.
3.20: And Ehud has come to him, and he is sitting in the upper chamber of the wall which he has for himself, and Ehud says, `A word of God I have to you;' and he rises from off the throne;
3.21: and Ehud puts forth his left hand, and takes the sword from off his right thigh, and strikes it into his belly;
3.22: and the haft also goes in after the blade, and the fat shuts on the blade, that he has not drawn the sword out of his belly, and it goes out at the fundament.
3.23: And Ehud goes out at the porch, and shuts the doors of the upper chamber upon him, and has bolted it;
3.24: and he has gone out, and his servants have come in, and look, and indeed, the doors of the upper chamber are bolted, and they say, `He is only covering his feet in the inner chamber of the wall.'
3.25: And they stay till confounded, and indeed, he is not opening the doors of the upper chamber, and they take the key, and open, and indeed, their lord is fallen to the earth--dead.
3.26: And Ehud escaped during their tarrying, and has passed by the images, and is escaped to Seirath.
3.27: And it comes to pass, in his coming in, that he blows with a trumpet in the hill-country of Ephraim, and go down with him do the sons of Israel from the hill-country, and he before them;
3.28: and he says to them, `Pursue after me, for Jehovah has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand;' and they go down after him, and capture the passages of the Jordan toward Moab, and have not permitted a man to pass over.
3.29: And they smite Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, all robust, and every one a man of valour, and not a man has escaped,
3.30: and Moab is humbled in that day under the hand of Israel; and the land rests eighty years.
3.31: And after him has been Shamgar son of Anath, and he smites the Philistines--six hundred men--with an ox-goad, and he saves--he also--Israel.

4.1: And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah when Ehud is dead,
4.2: and Jehovah sells them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who has reigned in Hazor, and the head of his host is Sisera, and he is dwelling in Harosheth of the Goyim;
4.3: and the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah, for he has nine hundred chariots of iron, and he has oppressed the sons of Israel mightily twenty years.
4.4: And Deborah, a woman inspired, wife of Lapidoth, she is judging Israel at that time,
4.5: and she is dwelling under the palm-tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Beth-El, in the hill-country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel go up to her for judgment.
4.6: And she sends and calls for Barak son of Abinoam, out of Kedesh-Naphtali, and says to him, `Has not Jehovah, God of Israel, commanded? go, and you have drawn toward mount Tabor, and have taken with you ten thousand men, out of the sons of Naphtali, and out of the sons of Zebulun,
4.7: and I have drawn to you, to the brook Kishon, Sisera, head of the host of Jabin, and his chariot, and his multitude, and have given him into your hand.'
4.8: And Barak says to her, `If you do go with me, then I have gone; and if you do not go with me, I do not go;'
4.9: and she says, `I do certainly go with you; only, surely your glory is not on the way which you are going, for into the hand of a woman does Jehovah sell Sisera;' and Deborah rises and goes with Barak to Kedesh.
4.10: And Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and he goes up--at his feet are ten thousand men--and Deborah goes up with him.
4.11: And Heber the Kenite has been separated from the Kenite, from the sons of Hobab father-in-law of Moses, and he stretches out his tent to the oak in Zaanaim, which is by Kedesh.
4.12: And they declare to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam has gone up to mount Tabor,
4.13: and Sisera calls all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who are with him, from Harosheth of the Goyim, to the brook Kishon.
4.14: And Deborah says to Barak, `Rise, for this is the day in which Jehovah has given Sisera into your hand; has not Jehovah gone out before you?' And Barak goes down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
4.15: And Jehovah destroys Sisera, and all the chariots, and all the camp, by the mouth of the sword, before Barak, and Sisera comes down from off the chariot, and flees on his feet.
4.16: And Barak has pursued after the chariots and after the camp, to Harosheth of the Goyim, and all the camp of Sisera falls by the mouth of the sword--there has not been left even one.
4.17: And Sisera has fled on his feet to the tent of Jael wife of Heber the Kenite, for peace is between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite;
4.18: and Jael goes out to meet Sisera, and says to him, `Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me, fear not;' and he turns aside to her, into the tent, and she covers him with a coverlet.
4.19: And he says to her, `Give me to drink, I pray you, a little water, for I am thirsty;' and she opens the bottle of milk, and gives him to drink, and covers him.
4.20: And he says to her, `Stand at the opening of the tent, and it has been, if any does come in, and has asked you, and said, Is there a man here? that you have said, There is not.'
4.21: And Jael wife of Heber takes the pin of the tent, and takes the hammer in her hand, and goes to him gently, and strikes the pin into his temples, and it fastens in the earth--and he has been fast asleep, and is weary--and he dies.
4.22: And indeed, Barak is pursuing Sisera, and Jael comes out to meet him, and says to him, `Come, and I show you the man whom you are seeking;' and he comes in to her, and indeed, Sisera is fallen--dead, and the pin in his temples.
4.23: And God humbles on that day Jabin king of Canaan before the sons of Israel,
4.24: and the hand of the sons of Israel goes, going on and becoming hard on Jabin king of Canaan, till that they have cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

5.1: And Deborah sings--also Barak son of Abinoam--on that day, saying: --
5.2: `For freeing freemen in Israel, For a people willingly offering themselves Bless you Jehovah.
5.3: Hear, you kings; give ear, you princes, I, to Jehovah, I--I do sing, I sing praise to Jehovah, God of Israel.
5.4: Jehovah, in Your going forth out of Seir, In Your stepping out of the field of Edom, Earth trembled, also the heavens dropped, Also thick clouds dropped water.
5.5: Hills flowed from the face of Jehovah, This one--Sinai--From the face of Jehovah, God of Israel.
5.6: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath--In the days of Jael--The ways have ceased, And those going in the paths go in crooked ways.
5.7: Villages ceased in Israel--they ceased, Till that I arose--Deborah, That I arose, a mother in Israel.
5.8: He chooses new gods, Then war is at the gates! A shield is not seen--and a spear Among forty thousand in Israel.
5.9: My heart is to the lawgivers of Israel, Who are offering themselves willingly among the people, Bless you Jehovah!
5.10: Riders on white asses--Sitters on a long robe--And walkers by the way--meditate!
5.11: By the voice of shouters Between the places of drawing water, There they give out righteous acts of Jehovah, Righteous acts of His villages in Israel, Then ruled in the gates have the people of Jehovah.
5.12: Awake, awake, Deborah; Awake, awake, utter a song; Rise, Barak, and take captive your captivity, Son of Abinoam.
5.13: Then him who is left of the honourable ones He caused to rule the people of Jehovah, He caused me to rule among the mighty.
5.14: Out of Ephraim their root is against Amalek. After you, Benjamin, among your peoples. Out of Machir came down lawgivers, And out of Zebulun those drawing with the reed of a writer.
5.15: And princes in Issachar are with Deborah, Yes, Issachar is right with Barak, Into the valley he was sent on his feet. In the divisions of Reuben, Great are the decrees of heart!
5.16: Why have you abode between the boundaries, To hear lowings of herds? For the divisions of Reuben, Great are the searchings of heart!
5.17: Gilead beyond the Jordan did tabernacle, And Dan--why does he sojourn in ships? Asher has abode at the haven of the seas, And by his creeks does tabernacle.
5.18: Zebulun is a people who exposed its soul to death, Naphtali also--on high places of the field.
5.19: Kings came--they fought; Then fought kings of Canaan, In Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo; Gain of money they took not!
5.20: From the heavens they fought: The stars from their highways fought with Sisera.
5.21: The brook Kishon swept them away, The brook most ancient--the brook Kishon. You do tread down strength, O my soul!
5.22: Then broken were the horse-heels, By pransings--pransings of its mighty ones.
5.23: Curse Meroz--said a messenger of Jehovah, Cursing, curse you its inhabitants, For they came not to the help of Jehovah, To the help of Jehovah among the mighty!
5.24: Blessed above women is Jael, Wife of Heber the Kenite, Above women in the tent she is blessed.
5.25: Water he asked--milk she gave; In a lordly dish she brought near butter.
5.26: Her hand to the pin she sends forth, And her right hand to the labourers' hammer, And she hammered Sisera--she smote his head, Yes, she smote, and it passed through his temple.
5.27: Between her feet he bowed--He fell, he lay down; Between her feet he bowed, he fell; Where he bowed, there he fell--destroyed.
5.28: Through the window she has looked out--Yes, she cries out--the mother of Sisera, Through the lattice: Wherefore is his chariot delaying to come? Wherefore tarried have the steps of his chariot?
5.29: The wise ones, her princesses, answer her, Yes, she returns her sayings to herself:
5.30: Do they not find? --they apportion spoil, A female--two females--for every head, Spoil of finger-work for Sisera, Spoil of embroidered finger-work, Finger-work--a pair of embroidered things, For the necks of the spoil!
5.31: So do all Your enemies perish, O Jehovah, And those loving Him are As the going out of the sun in its might!' and the land rests forty years.

6.1: And the sons of Israel do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah gives them into the hand of Midian seven years,
6.2: and the hand of Midian is strong against Israel, from the presence of Midian have the sons of Israel made for themselves the flowings which are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.
6.3: And it has been, if Israel has sowed, that Midian has come up, and Amalek, and the sons of the east, yes, they have come up against him,
6.4: and encamp against them, and destroy the increase of the land till your entering Gaza; and they leave no sustenance in Israel, either sheep, or ox, or ass;
6.5: for they and their cattle come up, with their tents; they come in as the fulness of the locust for multitude, and of them and of their cattle there is no number, and they come into the land to destroy it.
6.6: And Israel is very weak from the presence of Midian, and the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah.
6.7: And it comes to pass when the sons of Israel have cried to Jehovah, concerning Midian,
6.8: that Jehovah sends a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel, and he says to them, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I--I have brought you up out of Egypt, and I bring you out from a house of servants,
6.9: and I deliver you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all your oppressors, and I cast them out from your presence, and I give to you their land,
6.10: and I say to you, I am Jehovah your God, you do not fear the gods of the Amorite in whose land you are dwelling: --and you have not hearkened to My voice.'
6.11: And the messenger of Jehovah comes and sits under the oak which is in Ophrah, which is to Joash the Abi-Ezrite, and Gideon his son is beating out wheat in the wine-press, to remove it from the presence of the Midianites;
6.12: and the messenger of Jehovah appears to him, and says to him, `Jehovah is with you, O mighty one of valour.'
6.13: And Gideon says to him, `O, my lord--and Jehovah is with us! --and why has all this found us? and where are all His wonders which our fathers recounted to us, saying, Has not Jehovah brought us up out of Egypt? and now Jehovah has left us, and does give us into the hand of Midian.'
6.14: And Jehovah turns to him and says, `Go in this--your power; and you have saved Israel out of the hand of Midian--have not I sent you.'
6.15: And he says to him, `O, my lord, with which do I save Israel? indeed, my chief is weak in Manasseh, and I the least in the house of my father.'
6.16: And Jehovah says to him, `Because I am with you--you have smitten the Midianites as one man.'
6.17: And he says to Him, `If, I pray You, I have found grace in Your eyes, then You have done for me a sign that You are speaking with me.
6.18: Move not, I pray You, from this, till my coming in to You, and I have brought out my present, and put it before You;' and he says, `I--I do abide till your return.'
6.19: And Gideon has gone in, and prepares a kid of the goats, and of an ephah of flour unleavened things; the flesh he has put in a basket, and the broth he has put in a pot, and he brings out to Him, to the place of the oak, and brings it nigh.
6.20: And the messenger of God says to him, `Take the flesh and the unleavened things, and place on this rock--and the broth pour out;' and he does so.
6.21: And the messenger of Jehovah puts forth the end of the staff which is in His hand, and comes against the flesh, and against the unleavened things, and the fire goes up out of the rock and consumes the flesh and the unleavened things--and the messenger of Jehovah has gone from his eyes.
6.22: And Gideon sees that He is a messenger of Jehovah, and Gideon says, `Alas, Lord Jehovah! because that I have seen a messenger of Jehovah face to face!'
6.23: And Jehovah says to him, `Peace to you; fear not; you do not die.'
6.24: And Gideon builds there an altar to Jehovah, and calls it Jehovah-Shalom, to this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi-Ezrites.
6.25: And it comes to pass, on that night, that Jehovah says to him, `Take the young ox which is to your father, and the second bullock of seven years, and you have thrown down the altar of Baal which is to your father, and the shrine which is by it you do cut down,
6.26: and you have built an altar to Jehovah your God on the top of this stronghold, by the arrangement, and have taken the second bullock, and caused to ascend a burnt-offering with the wood of the shrine which you cut down.'
6.27: And Gideon takes ten men of his servants, and does as Jehovah has spoken to him, and it comes to pass, because he has been afraid of the house of his father, and the men of the city, to do it by day, that he does it by night.
6.28: And the men of the city rise early in the morning, and indeed, broken down has been the altar of Baal, and the shrine which is by it has been cut down, and the second bullock has been offered on the altar which is built.
6.29: And they say one to another, `Who has done this thing?' and they inquire and seek, and they say, `Gideon son of Joash has done this thing.'
6.30: And the men of the city say to Joash, `Bring out your son, and he dies, because he has broken down the altar of Baal, and because he has cut down the shrine which is by it.'
6.31: And Joash says to all who have stood against him, `You, do you plead for Baal? you--do you save him? he who pleads for him is put to death during the morning; if he is a god he himself does plead against him, because he has broken down his altar.'
6.32: And he calls him, on that day, Jerubbaal, saying, `The Baal does plead against him, because he has broken down his altar.'
6.33: And all Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east have been gathered together, and pass over, and encamp in the valley of Jezreel,
6.34: and the Spirit of Jehovah has clothed Gideon, and he blows with a trumpet, and Abi-Ezer is called after him;
6.35: and messengers he has sent into all Manasseh, and it also is called after him; and messengers he has sent into Asher, and into Zebulun, and into Naphtali, and they come up to meet them.
6.36: And Gideon says to God, `If You are Saviour of Israel by my hand, as You have spoken,
6.37: indeed, I am placing the fleece of wool in the threshing-floor: if dew is on the fleece alone, and on all the earth drought--then I have known that You do save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken;'
6.38: and it is so, and he rises early on the morrow, and presses the fleece, and wrings dew out of the fleece--the fulness of the bowl, of water.
6.39: And Gideon says to God, `Let not Your anger burn against me, and I speak only this time; let me try, I pray You, only this time with the fleece--let there be, I pray You, drought on the fleece alone, and on all the earth let there be dew.'
6.40: And God does so on that night, and there is drought on the fleece alone, and on all the earth there has been dew.

7.1: And Jerubbaal (he is Gideon) rises early, and all the people who are with him, and they encamp by the well of Harod, and the camp of Midian has been on the south of him, on the height of Moreh, in the valley.
7.2: And Jehovah says to Gideon, `Too many are the people who are with you for My giving Midian into their hand, lest Israel beautify itself against Me, saying, My hand has given salvation to me;
7.3: and now, call, I pray you, in the ears of the people, saying, Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and go early from mount Gilead;' and there turn back of the people twenty and two thousand, and ten thousand have been left.
7.4: And Jehovah says to Gideon, `Yet are the people too many; bring them down to the water, and I refine it for you there; and it has been, he of whom I say to you, This does go with you--he does go with you; and any of whom I say to you, This does not go with you--he does not go.'
7.5: And he brings down the people to the water, and Jehovah says to Gideon, `Every one who laps with his tongue of the water as the dog laps--you do set him apart; also every one who bows on his knees to drink.'
7.6: And the number of those lapping with their hand to their mouth is three hundred men, and all the rest of the people have bowed down on their knees to drink water.
7.7: And Jehovah says to Gideon, `By the three hundred men who are lapping I save you, and have given Midian into your hand, and all the people go, each to his place.'
7.8: And the people take the provision in their hand, and their trumpets, and every man of Israel he has sent away, each to his tents; and on the three hundred men he has kept hold, and the camp of Midian has been by him at the lower part of the valley.
7.9: And it comes to pass, on that night, that Jehovah says to him, `Rise, go down into the camp, for I have given it into your hand;
7.10: and if you are afraid to go down--go down, you and Phurah your young man, to the camp,
7.11: and you have heard what they speak, and afterwards are your hands strengthened, and you have gone down against the camp.' And he goes down, he and Phurah his young man, to the extremity of the fifties who are in the camp;
7.12: and Midian and Amalek, and all the sons of the east are lying in the valley, as the locust for multitude, and of their camels there is no number, as sand which is on the sea-shore for multitude.
7.13: And Gideon comes in, and indeed, a man is recounting to his companion a dream, and says, `Indeed, a dream I have dreamed, and indeed, a cake of barley-bread is turning itself over into the camp of Midian, and it comes in to the tent, and smites it, and it falls, and turns it upwards, and the tent has fallen.'
7.14: And his companion answers and says, `This is nothing save the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel; God has given into his hand Midian and all the camp.'
7.15: And it comes to pass, when Gideon hears the narration of the dream and its interpretation, that he bows himself, and turns back to the camp of Israel, and says, `Rise you, for Jehovah has given into your hand the camp of Midian.'
7.16: And he divides the three hundred men into three detachments, and puts trumpets into the hand of all of them, and empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers.
7.17: And he says to them, `Look at me, and thus do; and indeed, I am coming into the extremity of the camp--and it has been--as I do so you do;
7.18: and I have blown with a trumpet--I and all who are with me, and you have blown with trumpets, even you, round about all the camp, and have said, For Jehovah and for Gideon.'
7.19: And Gideon comes--and the hundred men who are with him--into the extremity of the camp, at the beginning of the middle watch (it has only just confirmed the watchmen), and they blow with trumpets--dashing in pieces also the pitchers which are in their hand;
7.20: and the three detachments blow with trumpets, and break the pitchers, and keep hold with their left hand on the lamps, and with their right hand on the trumpets to blow, and they cry, `The sword of Jehovah and of Gideon.'
7.21: And they stand each in his place, round about the camp, and all the camp runs, and they shout, and flee;
7.22: and the three hundred blow the trumpets, and Jehovah sets the sword of each against his companion, even through all the camp; and the camp flees to Beth-Shittah, at Zererath, to the border of Abel-Meholah, by Tabbath.
7.23: And the men of Israel are called from Naphtali, and from Asher, and from all Manasseh, and pursue after Midian.
7.24: And messengers has sent Gideon into all the hill-country of Ephraim, saying, `Come down to meet Midian, and capture before them the waters to Beth-Barah, and the Jordan;' and every man of Ephraim is called, and they capture the waters to Beth-Barah, and the Jordan,
7.25: and they capture two of the heads of Midian, Oreb, and Zeeb, and slay Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they have slain at the wine-vat of Zeeb, and they pursue to Midian; and the heads of Oreb and Zeeb they have brought in to Gideon beyond the Jordan.

8.1: And the men of Ephraim say to him, `What is this thing you have done to us--not to call for us when you did go to fight with Midian?' and they strive with him severely;
8.2: and he says to them, `What have I done now like you? are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the harvest of Abi-Ezer?
8.3: Into your hand has God given the heads of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what have I been able to do like you?' Then their temper desisted from off him in his speaking this thing.
8.4: And Gideon comes in to the Jordan, passing over, he and the three hundred men who are with him--wearied, and pursuing,
8.5: and he says to the men of Succoth, `Give, I pray you, cakes of bread to the people who are at my feet, for they are wearied, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna kings of Midian.'
8.6: And the heads of Succoth say, `Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we give to your host bread?'
8.7: And Gideon says, `Therefore--in Jehovah's giving Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand--I have threshed your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness, and with the threshing instruments.'
8.8: And he goes up from there to Penuel, and speaks to them thus; and the men of Penuel answer him as the men of Succoth answered.
8.9: And he speaks also to the men of Penuel, saying, `In my turning back in peace, I break down this tower.'
8.10: And Zebah and Zalmunna are in Karkor, and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand, all who are left of all the camp of the sons of the east; and those falling are a hundred and twenty thousand men, drawing sword.
8.11: And Gideon goes up the way of those who tabernacle in tents, on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smites the camp, and the camp was confident;
8.12: and Zebab and Zalmunna flee, and he pursues after them, and captures the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and all the camp he has caused to tremble.
8.13: And Gideon son of Joash turns back from the battle, at the going up of the sun,
8.14: and captures a young man of the men of Succoth, and asks him, and he describes to him the heads of Succoth, and its elders--seventy and seven men.
8.15: And he comes in to the men of Succoth, and says, `Indeed Zebah and Zalmunna, with whom you reproached me, saying, Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand that we give to your men who are wearied bread?'
8.16: And he takes the elders of the city, and the thorns of the wilderness, and the threshing instruments, and teaches by them the men of Succoth,
8.17: and the tower of Penuel he has broken down, and slays the men of the city.
8.18: And he says to Zebah and to Zalmunna, `How--the men whom you slew in Tabor?' and they say, `As you--so they, one--as the form of the king's sons.'
8.19: And he says, `My brethren--sons of my mother--they; Jehovah lives, if you had kept them alive--I had not slain you.'
8.20: And he says to Jether his first-born, `Rise, slay them;' and the young man has not drawn his sword, for he has been afraid, for he is yet a youth.
8.21: And Zebah says--also Zalmunna--`Rise you, and fall upon us; for as the man--his might;' and Gideon rises, and slays Zebah and Zalmunna, and takes their round ornaments which are on the necks of their camels.
8.22: And the men of Israel say to Gideon, `Rule over us, both you, and your son, and your son's son, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.'
8.23: And Gideon says to them, `I do not rule over you, nor does my son rule over you; Jehovah does rule over you.'
8.24: And Gideon says to them, `Let me ask of you a petition, and give you to me each the ring of his prey, for they have rings of gold, for they are Ishmaelites.'
8.25: And they say, `We certainly give;' and they spread out the garment, and cast there each the ring of his prey;
8.26: and the weight of the rings of gold which he asked is a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold, apart from the round ornaments, and the drops, and the purple garments, which are on the kings of Midian, and apart from the chains which are on the necks of their camels,
8.27: and Gideon makes it into an ephod, and sets it up in his city, in Ophrah, and all Israel go a-whoring after it there, and it is to Gideon and to his house for a snare.
8.28: And Midian is humbled before the sons of Israel, and have not added to lift up their head; and the land rests forty years in the days of Gideon.
8.29: And Jerubbaal son of Joash goes and dwells in his own house,
8.30: and to Gideon there have been seventy sons, coming out of his loin, for he had many wives;
8.31: and his concubine, who is in Shechem, has born to him--even she--a son, and he appoints his name Abimelech.
8.32: And Gideon son of Joash dies, in a good old age, and is buried in the burying-place of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abi-Ezrite.
8.33: And it comes to pass, when Gideon is dead, that the sons of Israel turn back and go a-whoring after the Baalim, and set over them Baal-Berith for a god;
8.34: and the sons of Israel have not remembered Jehovah their God, who is delivering them out of the hand of all their enemies round about,
8.35: neither have they done kindness with the house of Jerubbaal--Gideon--according to all the good which he did with Israel.

9.1: and Abimelech son of Jerubbaal goes to Shechem, to his mother's brethren, and speaks to them, and to all the family of the house of his mother's father, saying,
9.2: `Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the masters of Shechem, Which is good for you--the ruling over you of seventy men (all the sons of Jerubbaal), or the ruling over you of one man? --and you have remembered that I am your bone and your flesh.'
9.3: And his mother's brethren speak concerning him, in the ears of all the masters of Shechem, all these words, and their heart inclines after Abimelech, for they said, `He is our brother;'
9.4: and they give to him seventy silverings out of the house of Baal-Berith, and Abimelech hires with them men, vain and unstable, and they go after him;
9.5: and he goes into the house of his father at Ophrah, and slays his brethren, sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone; and Jotham, youngest son of Jerubbaal, is left, for he was hidden.
9.6: And all the masters of Shechem are gathered together, and all the house of Millo, and come and cause Abimelech to reign for king at the oak of the camp which is in Shechem;
9.7: and they declare it to Jotham, and he goes and stands on the top of mount Gerizim, and lifts up his voice, and calls, and says to them, `Hearken to me, O masters of Shechem, and God does hearken to you:
9.8: `The trees have diligently gone to anoint over them a king, and they say to the olive, Reign you over us.
9.9: And the olive says to them, Have I ceased from my fatness, by which they honour gods and men, that I have gone to stagger over the trees?
9.10: And the trees say to the fig, Come you, reign over us.
9.11: And the fig says to them, Have I ceased from my sweetness, and my good increase, that I have gone to stagger over the trees?
9.12: `And the trees say to the vine, Come you, reign over us.
9.13: And the vine says to them, Have I ceased from my new wine, which is rejoicing gods and men, that I have gone to stagger over the trees?
9.14: And all the trees say to the bramble, Come you, reign over us.
9.15: And the bramble says to the trees, If in truth you are anointing me for king over you, come, take refuge in my shadow; and if not--fire comes out from the bramble, and devours the cedars of Lebanon.
9.16: `And, now, if in truth and in sincerity you have acted, when you make Abimelech king; and if you have done good with Jerubbaal, and with his house; and if according to the deed of his hands you have done to him--
9.17: because my father has fought for you, and does cast away his life from him, and deliver you from the hand of Midian;
9.18: and you have risen against the house of my father to-day, and slay his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and cause Abimelech son of his handmaid to reign over the masters of Shechem, because he is your brother--
9.19: yes, if in truth and in sincerity you have acted with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, rejoice you in Abimelech, and he does rejoice--even he--in you;
9.20: and if not--fire comes out from Abimelech and devours the masters of Shechem and the house of Millo, and fire comes out from the masters of Shechem and from the house of Millo, and devours Abimelech.'
9.21: And Jotham hastes, and flees, and goes to Beer, and dwells there, from the face of Abimelech his brother.
9.22: And Abimelech is prince over Israel three years,
9.23: and God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and the masters of Shechem, and the masters of Shechem deal treacherously with Abimelech,
9.24: for the coming in of the violence to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, and of their blood to place it on Abimelech their brother, who slew them, and on the masters of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to slay his brethren.
9.25: And the masters of Shechem set for him ambushes on the top of the hills, and rob every one who passes over by them in the way, and it is declared to Abimelech.
9.26: And Gaal son of Ebed comes--also his brethren--and they pass over into Shechem, and the masters of Shechem trust in him,
9.27: and go out into the field, and gather their vineyards, and tread, and make praises, and go into the house of their god, and eat and drink, and revile Abimelech.
9.28: And Gaal son of Ebed says, `Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we serve him? is he not son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his commander? Serve you the men of Hamor father of Shechem, and wherefore do we serve him--we?
9.29: and oh that this people were in my hand--then I turn Abimelech aside;' and he says to Abimelech, `Increase your host, and come out.'
9.30: And Zebul, prince of the city, hears the words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger burns,
9.31: and he sends messengers to Abimelech deceitfully, saying, `Indeed, Gaal son of Ebed and his brethren are coming into Shechem, and indeed, they are fortifying the city against you;
9.32: and, now, rise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lay wait in the field,
9.33: and it has been, in the morning, about the rising of the sun, you do rise early, and have pushed against the city; and indeed, he and the people who are with him are going out to you--and you have done to him as your hand does find.'
9.34: And Abimelech rises, and all the people who are with him, by night, and they lay wait against Shechem--four detachments;
9.35: and Gaal son of Ebed goes out, and stands at the opening of the gate of the city, and Abimelech rises--also the people who are with him--from the ambush,
9.36: and Gaal sees the people, and says to Zebul, `Indeed, people are coming down from the top of the hills;' and Zebul says to him, `The shadow of the hills you are seeing like men.'
9.37: And Gaal adds yet to speak, and says, `Indeed, people are coming down from the high part of the land, and another detachment is coming by the way of the oak of Meonenim.'
9.38: And Zebul says to him, `Where is now your mouth, in that you say, Who is Abimelech that we serve him? is not this the people against which you have kicked? go out, I pray you now, and fight against it.'
9.39: And Gaal goes out before the masters of Shechem, and fights against Abimelech,
9.40: and Abimelech pursues him, and he flees from his presence, and many fall wounded--to the opening of the gate.
9.41: And Abimelech abides in Arumah, and Zebul casts out Gaal and his brethren from dwelling in Shechem.
9.42: And it comes to pass, on the morrow, that the people go out to the field, and they declare it to Abimelech,
9.43: and he takes the people, and divides them into three detachments, and lays wait in a field, and looks, and indeed, the people are coming out from the city, and he rises against them, and smites them.
9.44: And Abimelech and the detachments who are with him have pushed on, and stand at the opening of the gate of the city, and the two detachments have pushed against all who are in the field, and smite them,
9.45: and Abimelech has fought against the city all that day, and captures the city, and the people who are in it he has slain, and he breaks down the city, and sows it with salt.
9.46: And all the masters of the tower of Shechem hear, and go in to the high place of the house of the god Berith,
9.47: and it is declared to Abimelech that all the masters of the tower of Shechem have gathered themselves together,
9.48: and Abimelech goes up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people who are with him, and Abimelech takes the great axe in his hand, and cuts off a bough of the trees, and lifts it up, and sets it on his shoulder, and says to the people who are with him, `What you have seen I have done--haste, do you like it.'
9.49: And all the people also cut down each one his bough, and go after Abimelech, and set them at the high place, and burn by these the high place with fire, and also all the men of the tower of Shechem die, about a thousand men and women.
9.50: And Abimelech goes to Thebez, and encamps against Thebez, and captures it,
9.51: and a strong tower has been in the midst of the city, and there flee do all the men and the women, and all the masters of the city, and they shut it behind them, and go up on the roof of the tower.
9.52: And Abimelech comes to the tower, and fights against it, and draws nigh to the opening of the tower to burn it with fire,
9.53: and a certain woman does cast a piece of a rider on the head of Abimelech, and breaks his skull,
9.54: and he calls hastily to the young man bearing his weapons, and says to him, `Draw your sword, and you have put me to death, lest they say of me--A woman slew him;' and his young man pierced him through, and he dies.
9.55: And the men of Israel see that Abimelech is dead, and go each one to his place;
9.56: and God turns back the evil of Abimelech which he did to his father to slay his seventy brethren;
9.57: and all the evil of the men of Shechem has God turned back on their head, and come to them does the cursing of Jotham son of Jerubbaal.

10.1: And there rises after Abimelech, to save Israel, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, and he is dwelling in Shamir, in the hill-country of Ephraim,
10.2: and he judges Israel twenty and three years, and he dies, and is buried in Shamir.
10.3: And there rises after him Jair the Gileadite, and he judges Israel twenty and two years,
10.4: and he has thirty sons riding on thirty ass-colts, and they have thirty cities, (they call them Havoth-Jair to this day), which are in the land of Gilead;
10.5: and Jair dies, and is buried in Kamon.
10.6: And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and serve the Baalim, and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram, and the gods of Zidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the Bene-Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsake Jehovah, and have not served Him;
10.7: and the anger of Jehovah burns against Israel, and He sells them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the Bene-Ammon,
10.8: and they crush and oppress the sons of Israel in that year--eighteen years all the sons of Israel who are beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorite, which is in Gilead.
10.9: And the Bene-Ammon pass over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, and Israel has great distress.
10.10: And the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah, saying, `We have sinned against You, even because we have forsaken our God, and serve the Baalim.'
10.11: And Jehovah says to the sons of Israel, ` Have I not saved you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorite, from the Bene-Ammon, and from the Philistines?
10.12: And the Zidonians, and Amalek, and Maon have oppressed you, and you cry to Me, and I save you out of their hand;
10.13: and you--you have forsaken Me, and serve other gods, therefore I add not to save you.
10.14: Go and cry to the gods on which you have fixed; they--they save you in the time of your adversity.'
10.15: And the sons of Israel say to Jehovah, `We have sinned, do You to us according to all that is good in Your eyes; only deliver us, we pray You, this day.'
10.16: And they turn aside the gods of the stranger out of their midst, and serve Jehovah, and His soul is grieved with the misery of Israel.
10.17: And the Bene-Ammon are called together, and encamp in Gilead, and the sons of Israel are gathered together, and encamp in Mizpah.
10.18: And the people--heads of Gilead--say one to another, `Who is the man that does begin to fight against the Bene-Ammon? he is for head to all inhabitants of Gilead.'

11.1: And Jephthah the Gileadite has been a mighty man of valour, and he is son of a woman, a harlot; and Gilead begets Jephthah,
11.2: and the wife of Gilead bears to him sons, and the wife's sons grow up and cast out Jephthah, and say to him, `You do not inherit in the house of our father; for son of another woman are you.'
11.3: And Jephthah flees from the face of his brethren, and dwells in the land of Tob; and vain men gather themselves together to Jephthah, and they go out with him.
11.4: And it comes to pass, after a time, that the Bene-Ammon fight with Israel,
11.5: and it comes to pass, when the Bene-Ammon have fought with Israel, that the elders of Gilead go to take Jephthah from the land of Tob;
11.6: and they say to Jephthah, `Come, and you have been to us for captain, and we fight against the Bene-Ammon.'
11.7: And Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead, `Have not you hated me? and you cast me out from the house of my father, and wherefore have you come to me now when you are in distress?'
11.8: and the elders of Gilead say to Jephthah, `Therefore, now, we have turned back to you; and you have gone with us, and fought against the Bene-Ammon, and you have been to us for head--to all the inhabitants of Gilead.'
11.9: And Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead, `If you are taking me back to fight against the Bene-Ammon, and Jehovah has given them before me--I, am I to you for a head?'
11.10: And the elders of Gilead say to Jephthah, `Jehovah is hearkening between us--if according to your word we do not so.'
11.11: And Jephthah goes with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them for head and for captain, and Jephthah speaks all his words before Jehovah in Mizpeh.
11.12: And Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the Bene-Ammon, saying, `What--to me and to you, that you have come in to me, to fight in my land.'
11.13: And the king of the Bene-Ammon says to the messengers of Jephthah, `Because Israel took my land in his coming up out of Egypt, from Arnon, and to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan; and now, restore them in peace.'
11.14: And Jephthah adds yet and sends messengers to the king of the Bene-Ammon,
11.15: and says to him, `Thus said Jephthah, Israel took not the land of Moab, and the land of the Bene-Ammon,
11.16: for in their coming up out of Egypt, Israel goes in the wilderness to the Red Sea, and comes in to Kadesh,
11.17: and Israel sends messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Let me pass over, I pray you, through your land, and the king of Edom hearkened not; and also to the king of Moab has Israel sent, and he has not been willing; and Israel abides in Kadesh,
11.18: and he goes through the wilderness, and compasses the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and comes in at the rising of the sun of the land of Moab, and they encamp beyond Arnon, and have not come into the border of Moab, for Arnon is the border of Moab.
11.19: `And Israel sends messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and Israel says to him, Let us pass over, we pray you, through your land, to my place,
11.20: and Sihon has not trusted Israel to pass over through his border, and Sihon gathers all his people, and they encamp in Jahaz, and fight with Israel;
11.21: and Jehovah, God of Israel, gives Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smite them, and Israel possesses all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitant of that land,
11.22: and they possess all the border of the Amorite from Arnon, and to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness, and to the Jordan.
11.23: `And now, Jehovah, God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorite from the presence of His people Israel, and you would possess it!
11.24: That which Chemosh your god causes you to possess--do you not possess it? and all that which Jehovah our God has dispossessed from our presence, --it we do possess.
11.25: `And now, are you at all better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he at all strive with Israel? did he at all fight against them?
11.26: In Israel's dwelling in Heshbon and in its towns, and in Aroer and in its towns, and in all the cities which are by the sides of Arnon three hundred years--and wherefore have you not delivered them in that time?
11.27: And I--I have not sinned against you, and you are doing with me evil--to fight against me. Jehovah, the Judge, does judge to-day between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.'
11.28: And the king of the Bene-Ammon has not hearkened to the words of Jephthah which he sent to him,
11.29: and the Spirit of Jehovah is on Jephthah, and he passes over Gilead and Manasseh, and passes over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he has passed over to the Bene-Ammon.
11.30: And Jephthah vows a vow to Jehovah, and says, `If You do at all give the Bene-Ammon into my hand--
11.31: then it has been, that which at all comes out from the doors of my house to meet me in my turning back in peace from the Bene-Ammon--it has been to Jehovah, or I have offered up for it--a burnt-offering.'
11.32: And Jephthah passes over to the Bene-Ammon to fight against them, and Jehovah gives them into his hand,
11.33: and he smites them from Aroer, and to your going in to Minnith, twenty cities, and to the meadow of the vineyards--a very great smiting; and the Bene-Ammon are humbled at the presence of the sons of Israel.
11.34: And Jephthah comes into Mizpeh, to his house, and indeed, his daughter is coming out to meet him with timbrels, and with choruses, and save her alone, he has none, son or daughter.
11.35: And it comes to pass, when he sees her, that he rends his garments, and says, `Alas, my daughter, you have caused me greatly to bend, and you have been among those troubling me; and I--I have opened my mouth to Jehovah, and I am not able to turn back.'
11.36: And she says to him, `My father--you have opened your mouth to Jehovah, do to me as it has gone out from your mouth, after that Jehovah has done for you vengeance on your enemies, on the Bene-Ammon.'
11.37: And she says to her father, `Let this thing be done to me; desist from me two months, and I go on, and have gone down on the hills, and I weep for my virginity--I and my friends.'
11.38: And he says, `Go;' and he sends her away two months, and she goes, she and her friends, and she weeps for her virginity on the hills;
11.39: and it comes to pass at the end of two months that she turns back to her father, and he does to her his vow which he has vowed, and she knew not a man; and it is a statute in Israel:
11.40: from time to time the daughters of Israel go to talk to the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in a year.

12.1: And the men of Ephraim are called together, and pass over northward, and say to Jephthah, `Wherefore has you passed over to fight against the Bene-Ammon, and on us have not called to go with you? your house we burn over you with fire.'
12.2: And Jephthah says to them, `A man of great strife I have been (I and my people) with the Bene-Ammon, and I call you, and you have not saved me out of their hand,
12.3: and I see that you are not a saviour, and I put my life in my hand, and pass over to the Bene-Ammon, and Jehovah gives them into my hand--and why have you come up to me this day to fight against me?'
12.4: And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, and fights with Ephraim, and the men of Gilead smite Ephraim, because they said, `Fugitives of Ephraim are you Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim--in the midst of Manasseh.'
12.5: And Gilead captures the passages of the Jordan to Ephraim, and it has been, when any of the fugitives of Ephraim say, `Let me pass over,' and the men of Gilead say to him, `An Ephramite you?' and he says, `No;'
12.6: that they say to him, `Say, I pray you, Shibboleth;' and he says, `Sibboleth,' and is not prepared to speak right--and they seize him, and slaughter him at the passages of the Jordan, and there fall at that time, of Ephraim, forty and two chiefs.
12.7: And Jephthah judged Israel six years, and Jephthah the Gileadite dies, and is buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
12.8: And after him Ibzan of Beth-Lehem judges Israel,
12.9: and he has thirty sons and thirty daughters, he has sent without and thirty daughters has brought in to his sons from without; and he judges Israel seven years.
12.10: And Ibzan dies, and is buried in Beth-Lehem.
12.11: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judges Israel, and he judges Israel ten years,
12.12: and Elon the Zebulunite dies, and is buried in Aijalon, in the land of Zebulun.
12.13: And after him, Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judges Israel,
12.14: and he has forty sons, and thirty grandsons, riding on seventy ass-colts, and he judges Israel eight years.
12.15: And Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, dies, and is buried in Pirathon, in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekite.

13.1: And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah gives them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
13.2: And there is a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danite, and his name is Manoah, his wife is barren, and has not borne;
13.3: and a messenger of Jehovah appears to the woman, and says to her, `Indeed, I pray you, you are barren, and have not borne; when you have conceived, then you have borne a son.
13.4: And, now, take heed, I pray you, and do not drink wine, and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing,
13.5: for, indeed, you are conceiving and bearing a son, and a razor does not go up on his head, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the womb, and he does begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.'
13.6: And the woman comes and speaks to her husband, saying, `A man of God has come to me, and his appearance is as the appearance of a messenger of God, very fearful, and I have not asked him from where he is, and his name he has not declared to me;
13.7: and he says to me, Indeed, you are pregnant, and bearing a son, and now do not drink wine and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the womb till the day of his death.'
13.8: And Manoah makes entreaty to Jehovah, and says, `O, my Lord, the man of God whom You did send, let him come in, I pray you, again to us, and direct us what we do to the youth who is born.'
13.9: And God hearkens to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God comes again to the woman, and she is sitting in a field, and Manoah her husband is not with her,
13.10: and the woman hastes, and runs, and declares to her husband, and says to him, `Indeed, he has appeared to me--the man who came on that day to me.'
13.11: And Manoah rises, and goes after his wife, and comes to the man, and says to him, `Are you the man who spoke to the woman?' and he says, `I am.'
13.12: And Manoah says, `Now let your words come to pass; what is the custom of the youth--and his work?'
13.13: And the messenger of Jehovah says to Manoah, `Of all that I said to the woman let her take heed;
13.14: of anything which comes out from the wine-vine she does not eat, and wine and strong drink she does not drink, and any unclean thing she does not eat; all that I have commanded her she does observe.'
13.15: And Manoah says to the messenger of Jehovah, `Let us detain you, we pray you, and prepare before you a kid of the goats.'
13.16: And the messenger of Jehovah says to Manoah, `If you detain me--I do not eat of your bread; and if you prepare a burnt-offering--to Jehovah you do offer it;' for Manoah has not known that He is a messenger of Jehovah.
13.17: And Manoah says to the messenger of Jehovah, `What is your name? when your words come to pass, then we have honoured you.'
13.18: And the messenger of Jehovah says to him, `Why is this--you do ask for My name? --and it is Wonderful.'
13.19: And Manoah takes the kid of the goats, and the present, and offers on the rock to Jehovah, and He is doing wonderfully, and Manoah and his wife are looking on,
13.20: and it comes to pass, in the going up of the flame from off the altar toward the heavens, that the messenger of Jehovah goes up in the flame of the altar, and Manoah and his wife are looking on, and they fall on their faces to the earth,
13.21: and the messenger of Jehovah has not added again to appear to Manoah, and to his wife, then has Manoah known that He is a messenger of Jehovah.
13.22: And Manoah says to his wife, `We certainly die, for we have seen God.'
13.23: And his wife says to him, `If Jehovah were desirous to put us to death, He had not received from our hands burnt-offering and present, nor showed us all these things, nor as at this time caused us to hear anything like this.'
13.24: And the woman bears a son, and calls his name Samson, and the youth grows, and Jehovah does bless him,
13.25: and the Spirit of Jehovah begins to move him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

14.1: And Samson goes down to Timnath, and sees a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines,
14.2: and comes up and declares to his father, and to his mother, and says, `A woman I have seen in Timnath, of the daughters of the Philistines; and now, take her for me for a wife.'
14.3: And his father says to him--also his mother, `Is there not among the daughters of your brethren, and among all my people, a woman, that you are going to take a woman from the uncircumcised Philistines?' and Samson says to his father, `Take her for me, for she is right in my eyes.'
14.4: And his father and his mother have not known that from Jehovah it is, that a meeting he is seeking of the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines are ruling over Israel.
14.5: And Samson goes down--also his father and his mother, to Timnath, and they come to the vineyards of Timnath, and indeed, a lion's whelp roars at meeting him,
14.6: and the Spirit of Jehovah prospers over him, and he rends it as the rending of a kid, and there is nothing in his hand, and he has not declared to his father and to his mother that which he has done.
14.7: And he goes down and speaks to the woman, and she is right in the eyes of Samson;
14.8: and he turns back after some days to take her, and turns aside to see the carcase of the lion, and indeed, a company of bees are in the body of the lion--and honey.
14.9: And he takes it down on to his hands, and goes on, going and eating; and he goes to his father, and to his mother, and gives to them, and they eat, and he has not declared to them that from the body of the lion he took down the honey.
14.10: And his father goes down to the woman, and Samson makes there a banquet, for so the young men do;
14.11: and it comes to pass when they see him, that they take thirty companions, and they are with him.
14.12: And Samson says to them, `Let me, I pray you, put forth to you a riddle; if you certainly declare it to me in the seven days of the banquet, and have found it out, then I have given to you thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments;
14.13: and if you are not able to declare it to me, then you have given to me thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments.' And they say to him, `Put forth your riddle, and we hear it!'
14.14: And he says to them: `Out of the eater came forth meat, And out of the strong came forth sweetness;' and they were not able to declare the riddle in three days.
14.15: And it comes to pass, on the seventh day, that they say to Samson's wife, `Entice your husband, that he declare to us the riddle, lest we burn you and the house of your father with fire; to possess us have you called for us? is it not?'
14.16: And Samson's wife weeps for it, and says, `You have only hated me, and have not loved me; the riddle you have put forth to the sons of my people--and to me you have not declared it;' and he says to her, `Indeed, to my father and to my mother I have not declared it --and to you I declare it!'
14.17: And she weeps for it the seven days in which their banquet has been, and it comes to pass on the seventh day that he declares it to her, for she has distressed him; and she declares the riddle to the sons of her people.
14.18: And the men of the city say to him on the seventh day, before the sun goes in: --`What is sweeter than honey? And what stronger than a lion?' And he says to them: `Unless you had ploughed with my heifer, You had not found out my riddle.'
14.19: And the Spirit of Jehovah prospers over him, and he goes down to Ashkelon, and smites of them thirty men, and takes their armour, and gives the changes to those declaring the riddle; and his anger burns, and he goes up to the house of his father;
14.20: and Samson's wife becomes his companion's, who is his friend.

15.1: And it comes to pass, after some days, in the days of wheat-harvest, that Samson looks after his wife, with a kid of the goats, and says, `I go in to my wife, to the inner chamber;' and her father has not permitted him to go in,
15.2: and her father says, I certainly said, that you did certainly hate her, and I give her to your companion; is not her sister--the young one--better than she? Let her be, I pray you, to you, instead of her.'
15.3: And Samson says of them, `I am more innocent this time than the Philistines, though I am doing with them evil.'
15.4: And Samson goes and catches three hundred foxes, and takes torches, and turns tail to tail, and puts a torch between the two tails, in the midst,
15.5: and kindles fire in the torches, and sends them out into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burns it from heap even to standing corn, even to vineyard--olive-yard.
15.6: And the Philistines say, `Who has done this?' And they say, `Samson, son-in-law of the Timnite, because he has taken away his wife, and gives her to his companion;' and the Philistines go up, and burn her and her father with fire.
15.7: And Samson says to them, `Though you do thus, nevertheless I am avenged on you, and afterwards I cease!'
15.8: And he smites them hip and thigh--a great smiting, and goes down and dwells in the cleft of the rock Etam.
15.9: And the Philistines go up, and encamp in Judah, and are spread out in Lehi,
15.10: and the men of Judah say, `Why have you come up against us?' and they say, `To bind Samson we have come up, to do to him as he has done to us.'
15.11: And three thousand men of Judah go down to the cleft of the rock Etam, and say to Samson, `Have you now known that the Philistines are rulers over us? and what is this you have done to us?' And he says to them, `As they did to me, so I did to them.'
15.12: And they say to him, `To bind you we have come down--to give you into the hand of the Philistines.' And Samson says to them, `Swear to me, lest you fall upon me yourselves.'
15.13: And they speak to him, saying, No, but we certainly bind you, and have given you into their hand, and we certainly do not put you to death;' and they bind him with two thick bands, new ones, and bring him up from the rock.
15.14: He has come to Lehi--and the Philistines have shouted at meeting him--and the Spirit of Jehovah prospers over him, and the thick bands which are on his arms are as flax which they burn with fire, and his bands are wasted from off his hands,
15.15: and he finds a fresh jaw-bone of an ass, and puts forth his hand and takes it, and smites with it--a thousand men.
15.16: And Samson says, `With a jaw-bone of the ass--an ass upon asses--with a jaw-bone of the ass I have smitten a thousand men.'
15.17: And it comes to pass when he finishes speaking, that he casts away the jaw-bone out of his hand, and calls that place Ramath-Lehi;
15.18: and he thirsts exceedingly, and calls to Jehovah, and says, `You--You have given by the hand of Your servant this great salvation; and now, I die with thirst, and have fallen into the hand of the uncircumcised.'
15.19: And God cleaves the hollow place which is in Lehi, and waters come out of it, and he drinks, and his spirit comes back, and he revives; therefore has one called its name `The fountain of him who is calling,' which is in Lehi to this day.
15.20: And he judges Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.

16.1: And Samson goes to Gaza, and sees there a woman, a harlot, and goes in to her;
16.2: it is told to the Gazathites, saying, `Samson has come in here;' and they go round and lay wait for him all the night at the gate of the city, and keep themselves silent all the night, saying, `Till the light of the morning--then we have slain him.'
16.3: And Samson lies down till the middle of the night, and rises in the middle of the night, and lays hold on the doors of the gate of the city, and on the two side posts, and removes them with the bar, and puts on his shoulders, and takes them up to the top of the hill, which is on the front of Hebron.
16.4: And it comes to pass afterwards that he loves a woman in the valley of Sorek, and her name is Delilah,
16.5: and the princes of the Philistines come up to her, and say to her, `Entice him, and see in which his great power is, and in which we are able for him--and we have bound him to afflict him, and we--we give to you, each one, eleven hundred silverlings.'
16.6: And Delilah says to Samson, `Declare, I pray you, to me, in which your great power is, and with which you are bound, to afflict you.'
16.7: And Samson says to her, `If they bind me with seven green withs which have not been dried, then I have been weak, and have been as one of the human race.'
16.8: And the princes of the Philistines bring up to her seven green withs which have not been dried, and she binds him with them.
16.9: And the ambush is abiding with her in an inner chamber, and she says to him, `Philistines are upon you, Samson;' and he breaks the withs as a thread of tow is broken in its smelling fire, and his power has not been known.
16.10: And Delilah says to Samson, `Indeed, you have played upon me, and speak to me lies; now, declare, I pray you, to me, with which you are bound.'
16.11: And he says to her, `If they certainly bind me with thick bands, new ones, by which work has not been done, then I have been weak, and have been as one of the human race.'
16.12: And Delilah takes thick bands, new ones, and binds him with them, and says to him, `Philistines are upon you, Samson;' and the ambush is abiding in an inner chamber, and he breaks them from off his arms as a thread.
16.13: And Delilah says to Samson, `Hitherto you have played upon me, and do speak to me lies; declare to me with which you are bound.' And he says to her, `If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web.'
16.14: And she fixes it with the pin, and says to him, `Philistines are upon you, Samson;' and he awakes out of his sleep, and journeys with the pin of the weaving machine, and with the web.
16.15: And she says to him, `How do you say, I have loved you, and your heart is not with me? these three times you have played upon me, and have not declared to me in which your great power is.'
16.16: And it comes to pass, because she distressed him with her words all the days, and does urge him, and his soul is grieved to death,
16.17: that he declares to her all his heart, and says to her, `A razor has not gone up on my head, for a Nazarite to God I am from the womb of my mother; if I have been shaven, then has my power turned aside from me, and I have been weak, and have been as any of the human race.'
16.18: And Delilah sees that he has declared to her all his heart, and she sends and calls for the princes of the Philistines, saying, `Come up this time, for he has declared to me all his heart;' and the princes of the Philistines have come up to her, and bring up the money in their hand.
16.19: and she makes him sleep on her knees, and calls for a man, and shaves the seven locks of his head, and begins to afflict him, and his power turns aside from off him;
16.20: and she says, `Philistines are upon you, Samson;' and he awakes out of his sleep, and says, `I go out as time by time, and shake myself;' and he has not known that Jehovah has turned aside from off him.
16.21: And the Philistines seize him, and pick out his eyes, and bring him down to Gaza, and bind him with two brazen fetters; and he is grinding in the prison-house.
16.22: And the hair of his head begins to shoot up, when he has been shaven,
16.23: and the princes of the Philistines have been gathered together to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice; and they say, `Our god has given into our hand Samson our enemy.'
16.24: And the people see him, and praise their god, for they said, `Our god has given in our hand our enemy, and he who is laying waste our land, and who multiplied our wounded.'
16.25: And it comes to pass, when their heart is glad, that they say, `Call for Samson, and he does play before us;' and they call for Samson out of the prison-house, and he plays before them, and they cause him to stand between the pillars.
16.26: And Samson says to the young man who is keeping hold on his hand, `Let me alone, and let me feel the pillars on which the house is established, and I lean upon them.'
16.27: And the house has been full of men and of women, and there are all the princes of the Philistines, and on the roof are about three thousand men and women, who are looking on the playing of Samson.
16.28: And Samson calls to Jehovah, and says, `Lord Jehovah, remember me, I pray You, and strengthen me, I pray You, only this time, O God; and I am avenged--vengeance at once--because of my two eyes, on the Philistines.'
16.29: And Samson turns aside to the two middle pillars, on which the house is established, and on which it is supported, to the one with his right hand, and one with his left;
16.30: and Samson says, `Let me die with the Philistines,' and he inclines himself powerfully, and the house falls on the princes, and on all the people who are in it, and the dead whom he has put to death in his death are more than those whom he put to death in his life.
16.31: And his brethren come down, and all the house of his father, and lift him up, and bring him up, and bury him between Zorah and Eshtaol, in the burying-place of Manoah his father; and he has judged Israel twenty years.

17.1: And there is a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name is Micah,
17.2: and he says to his mother, `The eleven hundred silverlings which have been taken of yours, and of which you have sworn, and also spoken in my ears; indeed, the silver is with me, I have taken it;' and his mother says, `Blessed is my son of Jehovah.'
17.3: And he gives back the eleven hundred silverlings to his mother, and his mother says, `I had certainly sanctified the silver to Jehovah, from my hand, for my son, to make a graven image, and a molten image; and now, I give it back to you.'
17.4: And he gives back the money to his mother, and his mother takes two hundred silverlings, and gives them to a refiner, and he makes them a graven image, and a molten image, and it is in the house of Micah.
17.5: As to the man Micah, he has a house of gods, and he makes an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrates the hand of one of his sons, and he is to him for a priest;
17.6: in those days there is no king in Israel, each that which is right in his own eyes does.
17.7: And there is a young man of Beth-Lehem-Judah, of the family of Judah, and he is a Levite, and he is a sojourner there.
17.8: And the man goes out of the city, out of Beth-Lehem-Judah, to sojourn where he does find, and comes to the hill-country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, to work his way.
17.9: And Micah says to him, `From where do you come?' and he says to him, `A Levite am I, of Beth-Lehem-Judah, and I am going to sojourn where I do find.'
17.10: And Micah says to him, `Dwell with me, and be to me for a father and for a priest, and I give to you ten silverlings for the days, and a suit of garments, and your sustenance;' and the Levite goes in.
17.11: And the Levite is willing to dwell with the man, and the young man is to him as one of his sons.
17.12: And Micah consecrates the hand of the Levite, and the young man is to him for a priest, and he is in the house of Micah,
17.13: and Micah says, `Now I have known that Jehovah does good to me, for the Levite has been to me for a priest.'

18.1: In those days there is no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of the Danite is seeking for itself an inheritance to inhabit, for that has not fallen to it to that day in the midst of the tribes of Israel by inheritance.
18.2: And the sons of Dan send, out of their family, five men of them, men, sons of valour, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to traverse the land, and to search it, and they say to them, `Go, search the land;' and they come into the hill-country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodge there.
18.3: They are with the household of Micah, and they have discerned the voice of the young man, the Levite, and turn aside there, and say to him, `Who has brought you here? and what are you doing in this place? and what to you here?'
18.4: And he says to them, `Thus and thus has Micah done to me; and he hires me, and I am to him for a priest.'
18.5: And they say to him, `Ask, we pray you, at God, and we know whether our way is prosperous on which we are going.'
18.6: And the priest says to them, `Go in peace; over-against Jehovah is your way in which you go.'
